answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make identity expensive before it is trusted: agents put real capital in escrow (ivory towers of idle tokens get slashed) and earn reputation only by doing verifiable work, like navigating a karst landscape where every route is auditable on-chain. New agents that wander in from nowhere must stake more and earn attestations from established peers over time, so flooding the network with cheap fake identities costs more than the rewards they could ever extract.
